{"parentUuid":"6c1394d8-ffa4-4b57-98ed-8d2cb806efff","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"7f8cd928-07f9-44ea-a8a2-d1c8fed515d6","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0196Bmy4FkE1RAu7UMvsMR7T","type":"tool_result","content":"# Issue tracker: GitHub\n\nIssues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.\n- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.\n- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.\n- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body \"<answer>\"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.\n# Triage Labels\n\nThe skills speak in terms of five canonical triage roles. This file maps those roles to the actual label strings used in this repo's issue tracker.\n\n| Label in mattpocock/skills | Label in our tracker | Meaning                                  |\n| -------------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |\n| `needs-triage`             | `needs-triage`       | Maintainer needs to evaluate this issue  |\n| `needs-info`               | `needs-info`         | Waiting on reporter for more information |\n| `ready-for-agent`          | `ready-for-agent`    | Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent  |\n| `ready-for-human`          | `ready-for-human`    | Requires human implementation            |\n| `wontfix`                  | `wontfix`            | Will not be actioned                     |\n\nWhen a skill mentions a role (e.g. \"apply the AFK-ready triage label\"), use the corresponding label string from this table.\n\nEdit the right-hand column to match whatever vocabulary you actually use.\n.claude/hooks/ctx_compact_log.py\n.claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py\n.claude/hooks/ctx_statusline.py\n.claude/hooks/save_transcript.py\n.claude/settings.json\n.claude/skills/PINNED.md\n.env.example\n.gitignore\nCLAUDE.md\nCONTEXT.md\nREADME.md\nSECURITY-CHECKLIST.md\napp/__init__.py\napp/cli.py\napp/main.py\napp/publish.py\napp/settings.py\ndocs/adr/ADR-001-local-admin-static-public.md\ndocs/adr/ADR-002-stack.md\ndocs/agents/domain.md\ndocs/agents/issue-tracker.md\ndocs/agents/triage-labels.md\ndocs/handoff/.gitkeep\ndocs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md\ndocs/mp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md\ndocs/mp2-setup_context-threshold-hook_20260922.md\ndocs/process/.gitkeep\ndocs/screenshots/.gitkeep\nnotes/.gitkeep\nnotes/client-brief.md\nnotes/cms-field-notes.md\nnotes/setup_check.md\nnotes/token-budget-plan.md\nnotes/usage-ledger.csv\npyproject.toml\nscripts/check_submission.py\nscripts/seed_demo.py\nscripts/usage_report.py\ntemplates/admin/hello.html\ntemplates/base.html\ntemplates/public/home.html\ntests/conftest.py\ntests/test_ctx_guard.py\ntests/test_t00.py\ntests/test_usage_report.py\nuv.lock\n\"\"\"Shared test fixtures.\n\n`client` gives you the app. `client_as(role)` gives you a client that is logged\nin as a seeded user of that role — it works as soon as your login route exists,\nso access-control tests stay one line:\n\n    def test_editor_cannot_manage_users(client_as):\n        assert client_as(\"editor\").get(\"/admin/users\").status_code in (302, 403)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app.main import create_app\n\n# Matches scripts/seed_demo.py. Passwords come from the environment there; in\n# tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_USERS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"email\": \"admin@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\"},\n    \"editor\": {\"email\": \"editor@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\"},\n}\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client() -> TestClient:\n    return TestClient(create_app())\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client_as():\n    \"\"\"Return a factory: client_as(\"editor\") -> a logged-in TestClient.\"\"\"\n\n    def _login(role: str) -> TestClient:\n        user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n        c = TestClient(create_app())\n        response = c.post(\"/login\", data={\"email\": user[\"email\"],\n                                          \"password\": user[\"password\"]},\n                          follow_redirects=False)\n        if response.status_code == 404:\n            pytest.skip(\"No /login route yet — build the login ticket first.\")\n        assert response.status_code in (200, 302, 303), (\n            f\"Login as {role} failed with {response.status_code}\")\n        return c\n\n    return _login\n# ADR-001: The admin console runs locally; the public site is a static export\n\n**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n**Date:** 2026-09-22\n\n## Context\n\nA CMS needs a server, a database, and login. GitHub Pages serves static files\nonly: it cannot run Python and has no database. Students have two weeks and no\nhosting budget, and a first web application with real authentication is an\nattractive target the moment it is public.\n\n## Decision\n\nThe admin console (FastAPI + SQLite) runs on the student's own machine. A\n`cms publish` step renders the published content to static HTML in `site/`, which\nis deployed to GitHub Pages on the `gh-pages` branch.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Login, roles, and the database are never exposed to the internet.\n- The public site cannot have server-side features (search, comments) without a\n  different host; a stretch goal may add a live admin deploy behind a security gate.\n- Publishing is explicit: content changes are not live until `cms publish` runs,\n  which is a behaviour worth documenting for your client.\n- Relative paths become mandatory, because Pages serves the site from a subfolder.\n\n## Why this is an ADR\n\nIt is hard to reverse (it shapes every route, template, and deploy step) and it\nis surprising without context (most CMSes are servers). That is the bar; most\ndecisions do not meet it and belong in the spec or the glossary instead.\n# ADR-002: FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, with no frontend framework\n\n**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n**Date:** 2026-09-22\n\n## Context\n\nThe project has to be readable by someone who has never built a web application,\ngradable from a clean clone, and finishable in two weeks on a $20 plan. Options\nconsidered: Django (batteries included, but a large amount of generated code to\nread), Flask (similar to FastAPI here), a JavaScript stack (a second language and\na build step), and FastAPI with server-rendered templates.\n\n## Decision\n\nFastAPI with Jinja2 templates, SQLite for storage, argon2 for password hashing,\nand an HTML sanitizer for user Markdown. No frontend framework, no build step.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Every page is server-rendered, so \"view source\" shows what the code produced,\n  which makes debugging visible.\n- SQLite is a single file, so a grader can seed and inspect it easily. It is\n  gitignored; `scripts/seed_demo.py` rebuilds it.\n- No build step means the file you preview is the file that ships.\n- Interactive flourishes (live preview without reload, drag-and-drop) cost more\n  here than in a JavaScript stack. That is an accepted trade.\naccessibility\tBarrier affecting people with disabilities\t#f143ab\nbug\tSomething isn't working\t#d73a4a\ndocumentation\tImprovements or additions to documentation\t#0075ca\nduplicate\tThis issue or pull request already exists\t#cfd3d7\nenhancement\tNew feature or request\t#a2eeef\ngood first issue\tGood for newcomers\t#7057ff\nhelp wanted\tExtra attention is needed\t#008672\ninvalid\tThis doesn't seem right\t#e4e669\nquestion\tFurther information is requested\t#d876e3\nwontfix\tThis will not be worked on\t#ffffff","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"21e47425-921a-47ba-8bce-a708aa05b62d","timestamp":"2026-10-12T22:07:50.027Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"# Issue tracker: GitHub\n\nIssues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.\n- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.\n- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.\n- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body \"<answer>\"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.\n# Triage Labels\n\nThe skills speak in terms of five canonical triage roles. This file maps those roles to the actual label strings used in this repo's issue tracker.\n\n| Label in mattpocock/skills | Label in our tracker | Meaning                                  |\n| -------------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |\n| `needs-triage`             | `needs-triage`       | Maintainer needs to evaluate this issue  |\n| `needs-info`               | `needs-info`         | Waiting on reporter for more information |\n| `ready-for-agent`          | `ready-for-agent`    | Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent  |\n| `ready-for-human`          | `ready-for-human`    | Requires human implementation            |\n| `wontfix`                  | `wontfix`            | Will not be actioned                     |\n\nWhen a skill mentions a role (e.g. \"apply the AFK-ready triage label\"), use the corresponding label string from this table.\n\nEdit the right-hand column to match whatever vocabulary you actually use.\n.claude/hooks/ctx_compact_log.py\n.claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py\n.claude/hooks/ctx_statusline.py\n.claude/hooks/save_transcript.py\n.claude/settings.json\n.claude/skills/PINNED.md\n.env.example\n.gitignore\nCLAUDE.md\nCONTEXT.md\nREADME.md\nSECURITY-CHECKLIST.md\napp/__init__.py\napp/cli.py\napp/main.py\napp/publish.py\napp/settings.py\ndocs/adr/ADR-001-local-admin-static-public.md\ndocs/adr/ADR-002-stack.md\ndocs/agents/domain.md\ndocs/agents/issue-tracker.md\ndocs/agents/triage-labels.md\ndocs/handoff/.gitkeep\ndocs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md\ndocs/mp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md\ndocs/mp2-setup_context-threshold-hook_20260922.md\ndocs/process/.gitkeep\ndocs/screenshots/.gitkeep\nnotes/.gitkeep\nnotes/client-brief.md\nnotes/cms-field-notes.md\nnotes/setup_check.md\nnotes/token-budget-plan.md\nnotes/usage-ledger.csv\npyproject.toml\nscripts/check_submission.py\nscripts/seed_demo.py\nscripts/usage_report.py\ntemplates/admin/hello.html\ntemplates/base.html\ntemplates/public/home.html\ntests/conftest.py\ntests/test_ctx_guard.py\ntests/test_t00.py\ntests/test_usage_report.py\nuv.lock\n\"\"\"Shared test fixtures.\n\n`client` gives you the app. `client_as(role)` gives you a client that is logged\nin as a seeded user of that role — it works as soon as your login route exists,\nso access-control tests stay one line:\n\n    def test_editor_cannot_manage_users(client_as):\n        assert client_as(\"editor\").get(\"/admin/users\").status_code in (302, 403)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app.main import create_app\n\n# Matches scripts/seed_demo.py. Passwords come from the environment there; in\n# tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_USERS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"email\": \"admin@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\"},\n    \"editor\": {\"email\": \"editor@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\"},\n}\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client() -> TestClient:\n    return TestClient(create_app())\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client_as():\n    \"\"\"Return a factory: client_as(\"editor\") -> a logged-in TestClient.\"\"\"\n\n    def _login(role: str) -> TestClient:\n        user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n        c = TestClient(create_app())\n        response = c.post(\"/login\", data={\"email\": user[\"email\"],\n                                          \"password\": user[\"password\"]},\n                          follow_redirects=False)\n        if response.status_code == 404:\n            pytest.skip(\"No /login route yet — build the login ticket first.\")\n        assert response.status_code in (200, 302, 303), (\n            f\"Login as {role} failed with {response.status_code}\")\n        return c\n\n    return _login\n# ADR-001: The admin console runs locally; the public site is a static export\n\n**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n**Date:** 2026-09-22\n\n## Context\n\nA CMS needs a server, a database, and login. GitHub Pages serves static files\nonly: it cannot run Python and has no database. Students have two weeks and no\nhosting budget, and a first web application with real authentication is an\nattractive target the moment it is public.\n\n## Decision\n\nThe admin console (FastAPI + SQLite) runs on the student's own machine. A\n`cms publish` step renders the published content to static HTML in `site/`, which\nis deployed to GitHub Pages on the `gh-pages` branch.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Login, roles, and the database are never exposed to the internet.\n- The public site cannot have server-side features (search, comments) without a\n  different host; a stretch goal may add a live admin deploy behind a security gate.\n- Publishing is explicit: content changes are not live until `cms publish` runs,\n  which is a behaviour worth documenting for your client.\n- Relative paths become mandatory, because Pages serves the site from a subfolder.\n\n## Why this is an ADR\n\nIt is hard to reverse (it shapes every route, template, and deploy step) and it\nis surprising without context (most CMSes are servers). That is the bar; most\ndecisions do not meet it and belong in the spec or the glossary instead.\n# ADR-002: FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, with no frontend framework\n\n**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n**Date:** 2026-09-22\n\n## Context\n\nThe project has to be readable by someone who has never built a web application,\ngradable from a clean clone, and finishable in two weeks on a $20 plan. Options\nconsidered: Django (batteries included, but a large amount of generated code to\nread), Flask (similar to FastAPI here), a JavaScript stack (a second language and\na build step), and FastAPI with server-rendered templates.\n\n## Decision\n\nFastAPI with Jinja2 templates, SQLite for storage, argon2 for password hashing,\nand an HTML sanitizer for user Markdown. No frontend framework, no build step.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Every page is server-rendered, so \"view source\" shows what the code produced,\n  which makes debugging visible.\n- SQLite is a single file, so a grader can seed and inspect it easily. It is\n  gitignored; `scripts/seed_demo.py` rebuilds it.\n- No build step means the file you preview is the file that ships.\n- Interactive flourishes (live preview without reload, drag-and-drop) cost more\n  here than in a JavaScript stack. That is an accepted trade.\naccessibility\tBarrier affecting people with disabilities\t#f143ab\nbug\tSomething isn't working\t#d73a4a\ndocumentation\tImprovements or additions to documentation\t#0075ca\nduplicate\tThis issue or pull request already exists\t#cfd3d7\nenhancement\tNew feature or request\t#a2eeef\ngood first issue\tGood for newcomers\t#7057ff\nhelp wanted\tExtra attention is needed\t#008672\ninvalid\tThis doesn't seem right\t#e4e669\nquestion\tFurther information is requested\t#d876e3\nwontfix\tThis will not be worked on\t#ffffff","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"serverClassifierContext":{"request":"e9fc67ea-348a-47aa-8cb1-58574a309f89","context":{"git_state":{"cwd":"/Users/maysg/orca/iphs400-mp2-cms","root":"/Users/maysg/orca/iphs400-mp2-cms","branch":"main","default_branch":"main","status":{"clean":false,"counts":{"staged":0,"modified":2,"untracked":null,"untracked_normal":1},"porcelain":null,"truncated":false},"visibility":{"origin":{"host":"github.com","remote":"MaysG-creator/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"},"push_remote":"origin","remotes":[{"name":"origin","host":"github.com","remote":"MaysG-creator/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}],"visibility_cache":[{"host":"github.com","remote":"MaysG-creator/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}]}},"live_cwd":"/Users/maysg/orca/iphs400-mp2-cms","platform":"macos"}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"6c1394d8-ffa4-4b57-98ed-8d2cb806efff","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"classifier"},"session_id":"a121db57-1bee-4dbb-8856-8744e70c4142","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maysg/orca/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"a121db57-1bee-4dbb-8856-8744e70c4142","version":"2.1.296","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"aec34c30-52eb-411e-bfeb-82e2ef50a1f1","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfy78iSqztMaHoo1ezDML","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":""}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":743,"cache_read_input_tokens":79984,"output_tokens":4914,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":274},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":743,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":4914,"cache_read_input_tokens":79984,"cache_creation_input_tokens":743,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":743},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"thinkingDurationMs":2240,"thinkingDisplay":"updates","serverClassifierRequest":"aad5775a-d210-42cc-a420-991aeec76f98","apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011Cfy78hgUDQF4eXPpxpepe","requestedModel":"claude-sonnet-5-5","attributionSkill":"mattpocock-skills:to-spec","attributionPlugin":"mattpocock-skills","type":"assistant","uuid":"f9f02656-a2d8-45a1-89a8-e574f861cf17","timestamp":"2026-10-12T22:09:09.983Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":"medium","session_id":"a121db57-1bee-4dbb-8856-8744e70c4142","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maysg/orca/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"a121db57-1bee-4dbb-8856-8744e70c4142","version":"2.1.296","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"f9f02656-a2d8-45a1-89a8-e574f861cf17","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfy78iSqztMaHoo1ezDML","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01M4ZK7Nw6PmxZAyk6tz86yf","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/maysg/orca/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/tech-spec_web-cms_v1_sonnet5med_20261012.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nKenyon College Men's Soccer has no reliable place for fans, alumni, and players' families to find accurate game information. Today news comes through Instagram, which is hard to search and confusing for older relatives, and updates arrive in a random order. The team's student media members have average computer skills and need a simple way to write updates, but a wrong score or scorer on a public team site is worse than no site at all. The program needs a small CMS where several students can prepare content, one trusted person decides what goes public, and fans see a fast, readable, purple and white site that says when it was last updated.\n\n## Solution\n\nA local admin console (FastAPI, Jinja, SQLite) where one admin and a group of student editors log in, write updates and pages, and manage users, plus a `cms publish` step that exports only published content as static HTML for GitHub Pages. Editors can only produce drafts; the single admin reviews and publishes. The public site shows the newest updates on the home page, a navigation built from published pages (Schedule, Roster, Results/Record, History, About/Contact), and a last-updated date on everything. The admin console never goes on the internet.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As an editor, I want to log in with my own email and password, so that my work is attributed to me.\n2. As an editor, I want a clear message when my password is wrong, so that I know to retry rather than think the site is broken.\n3. As an admin, I want to log out, so that nobody else can use the shared machine under my name.\n4. As an editor, I want to log out, so that the next editor at the shared machine signs in as themselves.\n5. As an admin, I want every password stored only as a hash, so that a stolen database never reveals passwords.\n6. As an editor, I want to create an update with a title and a Markdown body, so that I can write up a game quickly.\n7. As an editor, I want the slug generated from the title automatically, so that I never have to think about URLs.\n8. As an editor, I want a duplicate slug to be resolved automatically, so that two updates with the same title do not collide.\n9. As an editor, I want a Markdown preview in the editor, so that I can check formatting before I save.\n10. As an editor, I want my new content saved as a draft, so that nothing reaches fans before the admin approves it.\n11. As an editor, I want to edit any draft, so that a teammate can fix a mistake on game night.\n12. As an editor, I want to delete my own drafts, so that abandoned drafts do not clutter the list.\n13. As an editor, I want to be blocked from deleting someone else's draft, so that nobody loses work by accident.\n14. As an editor, I want to be blocked from publishing, unpublishing, or editing published content, so that live content only changes with the admin's approval.\n15. As an editor, I want a clear \"not allowed\" screen when I try an admin-only action, so that I understand why it did not work.\n16. As an editor, I want to create and edit page drafts such as Schedule, Roster, or History, so that I can prepare content for the admin.\n17. As an editor, I want to filter the content list by status and by type, so that I can find drafts that need work.\n18. As an editor, I want a success or error message after every save, so that I know whether my change landed.\n19. As an editor, I want the admin navigation visible on every screen, so that I never get lost.\n20. As an admin, I want a dashboard showing counts of drafts, published updates, and pages, so that I see what needs review at a glance.\n21. As an admin, I want to filter the content list to drafts, so that I can review what editors wrote.\n22. As an admin, I want to publish a draft, so that it becomes eligible for the public site.\n23. As an admin, I want to unpublish published content, so that a wrong score can be pulled quickly.\n24. As an admin, I want to edit published content, so that I can correct a mistake.\n25. As an admin, I want to delete published content or pages, with a confirm step, so that I do not remove something live by accident.\n26. As an admin, I want to set each page's nav order, so that Schedule and Results appear before History and About.\n27. As an admin, I want to create a user with an email, a name, a role, and a starting password, so that a new media member can join.\n28. As an admin, I want to change a user's role, so that responsibilities can change.\n29. As an admin, I want to deactivate a user, so that a graduating media member can no longer log in.\n30. As a deactivated user, I want my past drafts and attribution kept, so that history is not rewritten.\n31. As an admin, I want the system to enforce exactly one admin, so that the club's single-admin rule is true in code.\n32. As an admin, I want a hand-over action that promotes another user and demotes me in one step, so that the role can pass on when I graduate.\n33. As an admin, I want to be prevented from deactivating or demoting myself outside of hand-over, so that the site is never left without an admin.\n34. As an admin, I want `cms publish` to render only published updates and pages, so that drafts never leave the database.\n35. As an admin, I want `cms publish` to remove content I unpublished or deleted from the exported site, so that stale content does not stay live.\n36. As an admin, I want `cms deploy` to push the export to the gh-pages branch, so that fans see the new content.\n37. As an admin, I want a short written runbook for publish and deploy, so that whoever inherits the role can do it.\n38. As a fan, I want the home page to list the newest published updates first with their dates, so that I see the latest news.\n39. As a fan, I want a navigation menu built from published pages, so that I can reach Schedule, Roster, Results, History, and About.\n40. As a fan, I want each update and page to show when it was last updated, so that I can judge whether it is current.\n41. As a fan, I want to read a match report with the verified score and scorers, so that I trust the numbers.\n42. As an alumnus, I want a History page about past titles and accomplishments, so that I can find the program's record.\n43. As a player's relative, I want a Roster page, so that I can find the player.\n44. As a fan on a phone, I want the public site and admin screens to fit without sideways scrolling, so that I can read them anywhere.\n45. As a fan, I want the site to look purple and white with a clear header, so that it feels like Kenyon.\n46. As any visitor, I want all links to work on the hosted site, so that I never hit a broken page.\n47. As any visitor, I want no script from a user's Markdown to run, so that the site is safe to open.\n48. As the admin, I want every state-changing form to carry a CSRF token, so that another website cannot act on my behalf.\n49. As a maintainer, I want sample content clearly marked as sample, so that no invented score ever looks real.\n50. As an anonymous visitor to the admin console, I want to be sent to the login page, so that nothing is exposed.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Architecture.** Follow ADR-001 and ADR-002: a local FastAPI app with server-rendered Jinja templates and SQLite, and a publish step that writes static HTML. No frontend framework and no build step.\n- **Vocabulary.** All code, templates, and tickets use the terms in `CONTEXT.md`: Update (stored as a post), Fixture, Match report, Page, Nav order, Draft, Published, Slug, Admin, Editor, Hand-over, Last updated.\n- **Users.** A user has an email, a display name, a password hash (argon2), a role (admin or editor), and an active flag. Deactivation sets the flag and never deletes the user, so authorship survives.\n- **Single admin.** Exactly one active admin exists at all times. Role changes cannot create a second admin, and the admin cannot demote or deactivate themselves. The only path is a hand-over action, which promotes the target and demotes the current admin atomically.\n- **Content.** Updates and Pages share the same core fields: title, slug, Markdown body, status (draft or published), author, created and updated timestamps. Pages add a nav order. Only two statuses exist.\n- **Slugs.** Generated from the title on first save, made unique automatically, and not editable by editors. Only the admin may change a slug.\n- **Permissions.** Editor: create content as drafts, edit any draft, delete own drafts, view the content list and dashboard. Editor may not publish, unpublish, edit or delete published content, delete another editor's draft, or reach user management. Admin: everything, including publish, unpublish, edit and delete published content, and user management. Admin-only routes return 403 for editors and redirect anonymous visitors to login.\n- **Session and login.** Cookie-based sessions. Login failures show one generic message. Deactivated users cannot log in.\n- **CSRF.** Every state-changing form carries a token that the server verifies, and a POST without a valid token is rejected.\n- **Markdown safety.** User Markdown is rendered and then sanitized with an allow-list, both in the admin preview and in the export, so script tags and event-handler attributes never execute.\n- **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts, a filterable content list (by status and by type), an editor with a Markdown preview, a user list, and persistent navigation. Every save shows a success or error message. The console is not themed beyond clear, plain styling.\n- **Publish.** `cms publish` reads only published rows and regenerates the export folder from scratch, so unpublished or deleted content disappears. Output uses relative paths only. The home page lists published updates newest first, the navigation is built from published pages by nav order, and each item shows its last-updated date. `cms deploy` pushes the export to the gh-pages branch. Both commands run from the terminal, and a short runbook is part of the documentation.\n- **Public look.** Purple and white, with a CSS-only banner header, readable at 390 px. No image files are required.\n- **Seed data.** The demo seed creates one admin, one editor, a few drafts, and a few published items. All content is clearly marked as sample, never realistic scores or stats. Credentials come from the environment.\n- **Assumptions.** A deactivated user keeps authorship and content. Updates are expected about an hour after a game. Editors use one shared machine for now.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **What a good test is.** It asserts external behavior only: a status code, a redirect, a page's visible text, a file in the export. It never asserts on internal functions, table layouts, or template structure.\n- **Seam 1: the HTTP app.** Every capability is tested through the FastAPI test client, using the existing `client` and `client_as(role)` helpers. This covers login and logout, roles and the editor 403 and anonymous redirect on every admin-only route, content CRUD and status changes, the dashboard and filters, preview, user management, hand-over, CSRF rejection, and sanitized preview output.\n- **Seam 2: the publish export.** Run the exporter into a temporary folder and assert on the generated files: only published content is present, drafts are absent, unpublished content disappears on re-export, no root-absolute paths, navigation order matches nav order, sanitized bodies, and a last-updated date on each item.\n- **Acceptance criteria.** Each ticket's acceptance criteria map to at least one named test so the review and grading can trace them.\n- **Prior art.** The template's existing T00 test and the `client_as` fixture and its docstring examples for access-control tests.\n- **Not tested.** Visual styling and the GitHub deploy itself are checked by hand and with screenshots at 1280 px and 390 px.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Comments and moderation.\n- Live in-game scores or any server-side feature on the public site.\n- WYSIWYG editors, drag-and-drop page builders, and multi-site.\n- Remote access for editors; for now the console runs on one machine (a later change, possibly the live admin deploy stretch).\n- A \"verified result\" workflow or required source field for scores.\n- Theming the admin console.\n- Photo uploads and categories/tags are wanted but not in the core build; see Further Notes.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Stretch goals, after the 7 core capabilities are green and reviewed:** photo uploads with alt text, and categories and tags (for example by season or opponent). Each gets its own `stretch` issue. Each is worth 1 extra-credit point and only counts if the base score is 70 or higher.\n- **Core ticket plan.** The 7 required capabilities should split into 7 to 9 vertical tickets, each demoable alone and touching data, route, template, and test.\n- **Accuracy rule.** The client's hard rule is that the site must never show false information. That is the reason for draft-only editors, a last-updated date, clearly marked sample content, and unpublish being fast for the admin.\n- **ADR candidate.** Enforcing exactly one admin may be recorded as an ADR; this is pending the author's decision.\n- **Open item outside this spec.** `notes/cms-field-notes.md` needs at least 5 observations from WordPress Playground (S1.1) before Stage 1.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":743,"cache_read_input_tokens":79984,"output_tokens":4914,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":274},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":743,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":4914,"cache_read_input_tokens":79984,"cache_creation_input_tokens":743,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":743},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01M4ZK7Nw6PmxZAyk6tz86yf":{"file_path":"/Users/maysg/orca/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/tech-spec_web-cms_v1_sonnet5med_20261012.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nKenyon College Men's Soccer has no reliable place for fans, alumni, and players' families to find accurate game information. As an admin, I want to create a user with an email, a name, a role, and a starting password, so that a new media member can join.\n28. As an admin, I want to change a user's role, so that responsibilities can change.\n29. As an admin, I want to deactivate a user, so that a graduating media member can no longer log in.\n30. As a deactivated user, I want my past drafts and attribution kept, so that history is not rewritten.\n31. As an admin, I want the system to enforce exactly one admin, so that the club's single-admin rule is true in code.\n32. As an admin, I want a hand-over action that promotes another user and demotes me in one step, so that the role can pass on when I graduate.\n33. As an admin, I want to be prevented from deactivating or demoting myself outside of hand-over, so that the site is never left without an admin.\n34. As an admin, I want `cms publish` to render only published updates and pages, so that drafts never leave the database.\n35. As an admin, I want `cms publish` to remove content I unpublished or deleted from the exported site, so that stale content does not stay live.\n36. As an admin, I want `cms deploy` to push the export to the gh-pages branch, so that fans see the new content.\n37. As an admin, I want a short written runbook for publish and deploy, so that whoever inherits the role can do it.\n38. As a fan, I want the home page to list the newest published updates first with their dates, so that I see the latest news.\n39. As a fan, I want a navigation menu built from published pages, so that I can reach Schedule, Roster, Results, History, and About.\n40. As a fan, I want each update and page to show when it was last updated, so that I can judge whether it is current.\n41. As a fan, I want to read a match report with the verified score and scorers, so that I trust the numbers.\n42. As an alumnus, I want a History page about past titles and accomplishments, so that I can find the program's record.\n43. As a player's relative, I want a Roster page, so that I can find the player.\n44. As a fan on a phone, I want the public site and admin screens to fit without sideways scrolling, so that I can read them anywhere.\n45. As a fan, I want the site to look purple and white with a clear header, so that it feels like Kenyon.\n46. As any visitor, I want all links to work on the hosted site, so that I never hit a broken page.\n47. As any visitor, I want no script from a user's Markdown to run, so that the site is safe to open.\n48. As the admin, I want every state-changing form to carry a CSRF token, so that another website cannot act on my behalf.\n49. As a maintainer, I want sample content clearly marked as sample, so that no invented score ever looks real.\n50. As an anonymous visitor to the admin console, I want to be sent to the login page, so that nothing is exposed.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Architecture.** Follow ADR-001 and ADR-002: a local FastAPI app with server-rendered Jinja templates and SQLite, and a publish step that writes static HTML. No frontend framework and no build step.\n- **Vocabulary.** All code, templates, and tickets use the terms in `CONTEXT.md`: Update (stored as a post), Fixture, Match report, Page, Nav order, Draft, Published, Slug, Admin, Editor, Hand-over, Last updated.\n- **Users.** A user has an email, a display name, a password hash (argon2), a role (admin or editor), and an active flag. Deactivation sets the flag and never deletes the user, so authorship survives.\n- **Single admin.** Exactly one active admin exists at all times. Role changes cannot create a second admin, and the admin cannot demote or deactivate themselves. The only path is a hand-over action, which promotes the target and demotes the current admin atomically.\n- **Content.** Updates and Pages share the same core fields: title, slug, Markdown body, status (draft or published), author, created and updated timestamps. Pages add a nav order. Only two statuses exist.\n- **Slugs.** Generated from the title on first save, made unique automatically, and not editable by editors. Only the admin may change a slug.\n- **Permissions.** Editor: create content as drafts, edit any draft, delete own drafts, view the content list and dashboard. Editor may not publish, unpublish, edit or delete published content, delete another editor's draft, or reach user management. Admin: everything, including publish, unpublish, edit and delete published content, and user management. Admin-only routes return 403 for editors and redirect anonymous visitors to login.\n- **Session and login.** Cookie-based sessions. Login failures show one generic message. Deactivated users cannot log in.\n- **CSRF.** Every state-changing form carries a token that the server verifies, and a POST without a valid token is rejected.\n- **Markdown safety.** User Markdown is rendered and then sanitized with an allow-list, both in the admin preview and in the export, so script tags and event-handler attributes never execute.\n- **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts, a filterable content list (by status and by type), an editor with a Markdown preview, a user list, and persistent navigation. Every save shows a success or error message. The console is not themed beyond clear, plain styling.\n- **Publish.** `cms publish` reads only published rows and regenerates the export folder from scratch, so unpublished or deleted content disappears. Output uses relative paths only. The home page lists published updates newest first, the navigation is built from published pages by nav order, and each item shows its last-updated date. `cms deploy` pushes the export to the gh-pages branch. Both commands run from the terminal, and a short runbook is part of the documentation.\n- **Public look.** Purple and white, with a CSS-only banner header, readable at 390 px. No image files are required.\n- **Seed data.** The demo seed creates one admin, one editor, a few drafts, and a few published items. All content is clearly marked as sample, never realistic scores or stats. Credentials come from the environment.\n- **Assumptions.** A deactivated user keeps authorship and content. Updates are expected about an hour after a game. Editors use one shared machine for now.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **What a good test is.** It asserts external behavior only: a status code, a redirect, a page's visible text, a file in the export. It never asserts on internal functions, table layouts, or template structure.\n- **Seam 1: the HTTP app.** Every capability is tested through the FastAPI test client, using the existing `client` and `client_as(role)` helpers. This covers login and logout, roles and the editor 403 and anonymous redirect on every admin-only route, content CRUD and status changes, the dashboard and filters, preview, user management, hand-over, CSRF rejection, and sanitized preview output.\n- **Seam 2: the publish export.** Run the exporter into a temporary folder and assert on the generated files: only published content is present, drafts are absent, unpublished content disappears on re-export, no root-absolute paths, navigation order matches nav order, sanitized bodies, and a last-updated date on each item.\n- **Acceptance criteria.** Each ticket's acceptance criteria map to at least one named test so the review and grading can trace them.\n- **Prior art.** The template's existing T00 test and the `client_as` fixture and its docstring examples for access-control tests.\n- **Not tested.** Visual styling and the GitHub deploy itself are checked by hand and with screenshots at 1280 px and 390 px.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Comments and moderation.\n- Live in-game scores or any server-side feature on the public site.\n- WYSIWYG editors, drag-and-drop page builders, and multi-site.\n- Remote access for editors; for now the console runs on one machine (a later change, possibly the live admin deploy stretch).\n- A \"verified result\" workflow or required source field for scores.\n- Theming the admin console.\n- Photo uploads and categories/tags are wanted but not in the core build; see Further Notes.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Stretch goals, after the 7 core capabilities are green and reviewed:** photo uploads with alt text, and categories and tags (for example by season or opponent). Each gets its own `stretch` issue. Each is worth 1 extra-credit point and only counts if the base score is 70 or higher.\n- **Core ticket plan.** The 7 required capabilities should split into 7 to 9 vertical tickets, each demoable alone and touching data, route, template, and test.\n- **Accuracy rule.** The client's hard rule is that the site must never show false information. That is the reason for draft-only editors, a last-updated date, clearly marked sample content, and unpublish being fast for the admin.\n- **ADR candidate.** Enforcing exactly one admin may be recorded as an ADR; this is pending the author's decision.\n- **Open item outside this spec.** `notes/cms-field-notes.md` needs at least 5 observations from WordPress Playground (S1.1) before Stage 1.\n"}},"serverClassifierRequest":"aad5775a-d210-42cc-a420-991aeec76f98","apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cfy78hgUDQF4eXPpxpepe","requestedModel":"claude-sonnet-5-5","attributionSkill":"mattpocock-skills:to-spec","attributionPlugin":"mattpocock-skills","type":"assistant","uuid":"269dc5de-7aa1-426b-b50c-b6a6bcb2a1b4","timestamp":"2026-10-12T22:09:38.994Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":"medium","session_id":"a121db57-1bee-4dbb-8856-8744e70c4142","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maysg/orca/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"a121db57-1bee-4dbb-8856-8744e70c4142","version":"2.1.296","gitBranch":"main"}

Today news comes through Instagram, which is hard to search and confusing for older relatives, and updates arrive in a random order. The team's student media members have average computer skills and need a simple way to write updates, but a wrong score or scorer on a public team site is worse than no site at all. The program needs a small CMS where several students can prepare content, one trusted person decides what goes public, and fans see a fast, readable, purple and white site that says when it was last updated.\n\n## Solution\n\nA local admin console (FastAPI, Jinja, SQLite) where one admin and a group of student editors log in, write updates and pages, and manage users, plus a `cms publish` step that exports only published content as static HTML for GitHub Pages. Editors can only produce drafts; the single admin reviews and publishes. The public site shows the newest updates on the home page, a navigation built from published pages (Schedule, Roster, Results/Record, History, About/Contact), and a last-updated date on everything. The admin console never goes on the internet.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As an editor, I want to log in with my own email and password, so that my work is attributed to me.\n2. As an editor, I want a clear message when my password is wrong, so that I know to retry rather than think the site is broken.\n3. As an admin, I want to log out, so that nobody else can use the shared machine under my name.\n4. As an editor, I want to log out, so that the next editor at the shared machine signs in as themselves.\n5. As an admin, I want every password stored only as a hash, so that a stolen database never reveals passwords.\n6. As an editor, I want to create an update with a title and a Markdown body, so that I can write up a game quickly.\n7. As an editor, I want the slug generated from the title automatically, so that I never have to think about URLs.\n8. As an editor, I want a duplicate slug to be resolved automatically, so that two updates with the same title do not collide.\n9. As an editor, I want a Markdown preview in the editor, so that I can check formatting before I save.\n10. As an editor, I want my new content saved as a draft, so that nothing reaches fans before the admin approves it.\n11. As an editor, I want to edit any draft, so that a teammate can fix a mistake on game night.\n12. As an editor, I want to delete my own drafts, so that abandoned drafts do not clutter the list.\n13. As an editor, I want to be blocked from deleting someone else's draft, so that nobody loses work by accident.\n14. As an editor, I want to be blocked from publishing, unpublishing, or editing published content, so that live content only changes with the admin's approval.\n15. As an editor, I want a clear \"not allowed\" screen when I try an admin-only action, so that I understand why it did not work.\n16. As an editor, I want to create and edit page drafts such as Schedule, Roster, or History, so that I can prepare content for the admin.\n17. As an editor, I want to filter the content list by status and by type, so that I can find drafts that need work.\n18. As an editor, I want a success or error message after every save, so that I know whether my change landed.\n19. As an editor, I want the admin navigation visible on every screen, so that I never get lost.\n20. As an admin, I want a dashboard showing counts of drafts, published updates, and pages, so that I see what needs review at a glance.\n21. As an admin, I want to filter the content list to drafts, so that I can review what editors wrote.\n22. As an admin, I want to publish a draft, so that it becomes eligible for the public site.\n23. As an admin, I want to unpublish published content, so that a wrong score can be pulled quickly.\n24. As an admin, I want to edit published content, so that I can correct a mistake.\n25. As an admin, I want to delete published content or pages, with a confirm step, so that I do not remove something live by accident.\n26. As an admin, I want a hand-over action that promotes another user and demotes me in one step, so that the role can pass on when I graduate.\n33. As an admin, I want to be prevented from deactivating or demoting myself outside of hand-over, so that the site is never left without an admin.\n34. {"parentUuid":"76cf7cff-a7fa-404d-8511-5a2ad13c4cf3","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"148a994f-fa8b-4e78-af83-c505055e67fe","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/maysg/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/to-tickets\n\n# To Tickets\n\nBreak a plan, spec, or conversation into a set of **tickets**: tracer-bullet vertical slices, each declaring the tickets that **block** it.\n\nThe issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Gather context\n\nWork from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes a reference (a spec path, an issue number or URL) as an argument, fetch it and read its full body and comments.\n\n### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)\n\nIf you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Ticket titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\nLook for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. \"Make the change easy, then make the easy change.\"\n\n### 3. Draft vertical slices\n\nBreak the work into **tracer bullet** tickets.\n\n<vertical-slice-rules>\n\n- Each slice cuts a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests): vertical, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer\n- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own\n- Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window\n- Any prefactoring should be done first\n\n</vertical-slice-rules>\n\nGive each ticket its **blocking edges**: the other tickets that must complete before it can start. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.\n\n**Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change (rename a column, retype a shared symbol) whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket; green is promised only there.\n\n### 4. Quiz the user\n\nPresent the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each ticket, show:\n\n- **Title**: short descriptive name\n- **Blocked by**: which other tickets (if any) must complete first\n- **What it delivers**: the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work\n\nAsk the user:\n\n- Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)\n- Are the blocking edges correct: does each ticket only depend on tickets that genuinely gate it?\n- Should any tickets be merged or split further?\n\nIterate until the user approves the breakdown.\n\n### 5. Publish the tickets to the configured tracker\n\nPublish the approved tickets. **How** depends on the tracker `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` configured; the tickets are the same either way, only the shape of the blocking edges changes:\n\n- **Local files** → write one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first). Each file's \"Blocked by\" lists the numbers/titles it depends on. Use the per-ticket file template below: one ticket per file, never a single combined file.\n- **A real issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, …)** → publish one issue per ticket in dependency order (blockers first) so each ticket's blocking edges can reference real identifiers. Use the platform's native blocking / sub-issue relationship where it has one; otherwise set each ticket's \"Blocked by\" to the blocking issues. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label unless instructed otherwise; the tickets are agent-grabbable by construction.\n\nWork the **frontier**: any ticket whose blockers are all done. For a purely linear chain that means top to bottom.\n\nDo NOT close or modify any parent issue.\n\n<local-ticket-template>\n\n# <NN>: <Ticket title>\n\n**What to build:** the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective, not a layer-by-layer implementation list.\n\n**Blocked by:** the numbers/titles of the tickets that gate this one, or \"None (can start immediately)\".\n\n**Status:** ready-for-agent\n\n- [ ] Acceptance criterion 1\n- [ ] Acceptance criterion 2\n\n</local-ticket-template>\n\n<issue-template>\n\n## Parent\n\nA reference to the parent issue on the tracker (if the source was an existing issue, otherwise omit this section).\n\n## What to build\n\nThe end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective, not layer-by-layer implementation.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Criterion 1\n- [ ] Criterion 2\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- A reference to each blocking ticket, or \"None (can start immediately)\".\n\n</issue-template>\n\nIn either form, avoid specific file paths or code snippets: they go stale fast. Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Trim to the decision-rich parts, not a working demo, just the important bits.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"4166a468-55fe-4830-a9ca-2e48a0ff4a23","timestamp":"2026-10-12T22:13:08.618Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maysg/orca/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"a121db57-1bee-4dbb-8856-8744e70c4142","version":"2.1.296","gitBranch":"main"}

That is the whole skeleton — it exists so you can prove the stack\nruns before you build anything on it.\n\nAdd your routes in their own modules (app/routes/posts.py and so on) and include\nthem here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import settings\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n\n    @app.get(\"/admin\")\n    def admin_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/hello.html\", {\"title\": \"Admin\"}\n        )\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    # Your ticket work plugs in here, e.g.\n    #   from app.routes import posts\n    #   app.include_router(posts.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n\"\"\"The `cms` command: serve, publish, deploy.\n\n    uv run cms serve      # admin console + public preview at http://localhost:8000\n    uv run cms publish    # render site/ from published content\n    uv run cms deploy     # push site/ to the gh-pages branch (Pages serves it)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\n    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\n    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\n    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.command == \"serve\":\n        import uvicorn\n\n        uvicorn.run(\"app.main:app\", port=args.port, reload=args.reload)\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"publish\":\n        out = render_site()\n        print(f\"Wrote {out}. Preview it with:  python3 -m http.server -d {out} 8001\")\n        return 0\n\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Create demo data so a grader (and you) can use the CMS immediately.\n\n    uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py\n\nT00 has nothing to seed. As you build content types, extend this so it creates:\n  - one admin and one editor (passwords read from .env, never hard-coded)\n  - a few posts and pages, at least one draft and one published\n\nThe rubric expects this to run clean on a fresh clone with .env.example values\n(item E4), because the database itself is never committed.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    admin_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\")\n    editor_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\")\n    if not admin_pw or not editor_pw:\n        print(\"Set CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD in .env \"\n              \"(copy .env.example).\")\n        return 1\n\n    # TODO (your tickets): create the users, then the demo content.\n    print(\"Nothing to seed yet: no content types exist. \"\n          \"Extend scripts/seed_demo.py as you build T01+.\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"a96f2e01-cc70-4e0b-9da6-0af95e346742","timestamp":"2026-10-12T22:13:20.226Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nT00 (already done): the admin console answers at /admin and the public site\nanswers at /. {"parentUuid":"970a4f35-6499-4801-ba20-43ec639f0d55","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfy7dBDCMd7MEMuHiy9v7","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_017BBeHvFVLtekcymsQcVkbD","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maysg-orca-iphs400-mp2-cms/a121db57-1bee-4dbb-8856-8744e70c4142/scratchpad && mkdir -p $S && \nmk() { gh issue create --title \"$1\" --label ticket --label ready-for-agent --body-file \"$2\"; }\ncat > $S/t01.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\nSpec: #1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe seeded admin and editor can log in with their own email and password, and log out. Passwords are stored only as argon2 hashes. A wrong password is refused with a clear message, and an anonymous visitor to any admin screen is sent to the login page. The demo seed creates one admin and one editor from environment values. Every state-changing form, starting with login and logout, carries a CSRF token that the server checks.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The seeded admin and the seeded editor can each log in and are then logged out by the logout action\n- [ ] A wrong password is refused and shows an error message\n- [ ] An anonymous visitor to /admin is redirected to the login page\n- [ ] The stored password for each seeded user is an argon2 hash, never plain text, and no password is logged\n- [ ] A login or logout POST without a valid CSRF token is rejected\n- [ ] A deactivated user (active flag off) cannot log in\n- [ ] The seed script runs clean from the example environment values and creates the admin and editor\n- [ ] Login and the admin screen fit a 390 px wide screen with no sideways scrolling\n\n## Blocked by\n\nNone (can start immediately)\nEOF\ncat > $S/t02.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\nSpec: #1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe admin can create and edit an Update (a team news item) in an admin shell with persistent navigation. The title becomes an automatic slug that stays unique. The editor shows a Markdown preview that is sanitized, and every save shows a success or error message. New updates are always drafts and are visible only in the admin console.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The admin can create an update with a title and Markdown body; it is saved as a draft with author and created/updated timestamps\n- [ ] The slug is generated from the title, and a second update with the same title gets a different unique slug\n- [ ] The admin can edit an update and the change persists across a server restart\n- [ ] The editor shows a Markdown preview, and a body containing a script tag or an onerror attribute does not execute in the preview\n- [ ] A success message follows a good save and an error message follows a bad one (for example an empty title)\n- [ ] The admin navigation is visible on every admin screen\n- [ ] Every form carries a CSRF token and a POST without one is rejected\n- [ ] Anonymous visitors are redirected to login on these routes\n- [ ] The editor screen fits 390 px wide with no sideways scrolling\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #2 (T01: Log in and out)\nEOF\ncat > $S/t03.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\nSpec: #1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe admin can publish and unpublish an update, and `cms publish` renders only published updates into a static site: a home page listing updates newest first with a last-updated date, a purple and white CSS-only banner header, and relative paths only. `cms deploy` pushes the result to GitHub Pages, so a fan can open the live site and see the published update. A short runbook explains publish and deploy for whoever holds the admin role. This is the thin end-to-end path from write to live.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The admin can publish a draft and unpublish a published update, and the status persists across a server restart\n- [ ] `cms publish` exports only published updates; drafts and unpublished updates never appear in the exported files\n- [ ] Re-running `cms publish` after an unpublish removes that update from the exported site\n- [ ] The exported home page lists published updates newest first, each with its last-updated date\n- [ ] The exported site contains no root-absolute paths in href or src attributes, and all internal links resolve\n- [ ] Update bodies in the export are sanitized, so a script tag and an onerror attribute do not execute\n- [ ] The public site uses the purple and white look with a banner header and has no sideways scrolling at 390 px\n- [ ] After `cms deploy`, the Pages URL over HTTPS shows at least one published update\n- [ ] A short runbook describes publish and deploy step by step\n- [ ] Publish and unpublish are POST forms with CSRF tokens\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #3 (T02: Admin writes update drafts)\nEOF\ncat > $S/t04.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\nSpec: #1\n\n## What to build\n\nEditors become draft-only. An editor can create updates, edit any draft, and delete only their own drafts; they cannot publish, unpublish, or edit or delete published content. The admin can delete published content after a confirm step, and the next `cms publish` removes it from the site. Any admin-only action an editor tries leads to a clear \"not allowed\" screen, and anonymous visitors go to login.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An editor can create an update, and it is saved as a draft\n- [ ] An editor can edit any draft, including one written by someone else\n- [ ] An editor can delete their own draft but gets a refusal when deleting another editor's draft\n- [ ] An editor cannot publish or unpublish, and cannot edit or delete published content (403 or redirect to the refused screen)\n- [ ] The admin can delete published content after a confirm step; deleted content is gone after the next `cms publish`\n- [ ] Every admin-only route returns 403 or a redirect for an editor, and redirects an anonymous visitor to login (tests cover every such route)\n- [ ] The refused screen explains what is not allowed and fits 390 px wide\n- [ ] All new forms carry a CSRF token and reject a POST without one\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #3 (T02: Admin writes update drafts)\nEOF\ncat > $S/t05.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\nSpec: #1\n\n## What to build\n\nPages (Schedule, Roster, Results/Record, History, About/Contact) work like updates: same fields, draft and publish rules, and permissions. In addition, each page has a nav order set by the admin. Published pages become the public navigation in the exported site, in nav order, and each page shows its last-updated date.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An editor can create and edit a page as a draft, and only the admin can publish, unpublish, or delete it\n- [ ] A page has the same fields as an update (title, auto slug, sanitized Markdown, status, author, timestamps) plus a nav order that only the admin can set\n- [ ] Create, edit, publish, unpublish, and delete for pages all persist across a server restart\n- [ ] After `cms publish`, published pages appear in the navigation of every exported page, in nav order; drafts do not\n- [ ] An exported page shows its last-updated date\n- [ ] The navigation uses relative paths only and every nav link resolves\n- [ ] Page forms carry CSRF tokens and editors get the refused screen on admin-only page actions\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #4 (T03: Publish an update to the live site)\n- #5 (T04: Editors are draft-only)\nEOF\ncat > $S/t06.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\nSpec: #1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe admin console gets a dashboard that shows counts (drafts, published updates, pages) and a content list of updates and pages that can be filtered by status and by type, for both admin and editor.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The dashboard shows counts of drafts, published updates, and pages that match the data\n- [ ] The content list shows updates and pages together with title, type, status, author, and last-updated date\n- [ ] The list filters by status (draft or published) and by type (update or page), and the filters combine\n- [ ] A filter with no matches shows a clear empty message\n- [ ] Both admin and editor can see the dashboard and list, and anonymous visitors are redirected to login\n- [ ] The dashboard and list fit 390 px wide with no sideways scrolling\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #6 (T05: Pages with nav order)\nEOF\ncat > $S/t07.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\nSpec: #1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe admin can manage users: create a user with an email, name, role, and starting password; change a user's role; and deactivate a user, who then cannot log in. Exactly one admin exists at all times, so a second admin can never be created by changing a role, and the admin cannot demote or deactivate themselves. A hand-over action promotes another user to admin and demotes the current admin in one step. Editors cannot reach any of this.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The admin can create a user with a role, and the new user can log in; their password is stored as an argon2 hash\n- [ ] The admin can change a user's role between editor and a permitted value without ever producing two active admins\n- [ ] The admin can deactivate a user, and that user can no longer log in but keeps authorship of their content\n- [ ] The admin cannot demote or deactivate themselves outside of hand-over\n- [ ] Hand-over promotes the chosen user and demotes the current admin in one step, leaving exactly one admin\n- [ ] An editor gets 403 or a redirect on every user-management route, and anonymous visitors are redirected to login\n- [ ] All user-management forms carry CSRF tokens and reject a POST without one\n- [ ] The user list and forms fit 390 px wide with no sideways scrolling\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #5 (T04: Editors are draft-only)\nEOF\nmk \"T01: Log in and out\" $S/t01.md && mk \"T02: \"$1\" --label ticket --label ready-for-agent --body-file \"$2\"; }\ncat > $S/t01.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\nSpec: #1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe seeded admin and editor can log in with their own email and password, and log out. Passwords are stored only as argon2 hashes. A wrong password is refused with a clear message, and an anonymous visitor to any admin screen is sent to the login page. The demo seed creates one admin and one editor from environment values. Every state-changing form, starting with login and logout, carries a CSRF token that the server checks.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The seeded admin and the seeded editor can each log in and are then logged out by the logout action\n- [ ] A wrong password is refused and shows an error message\n- [ ] An anonymous visitor to /admin is redirected to the login page\n- [ ] The stored password for each seeded user is an argon2 hash, never plain text, and no password is logged\n- [ ] A login or logout POST without a valid CSRF token is rejected\n- [ ] A deactivated user (active flag off) cannot log in\n- [ ] The seed script runs clean from the example environment values and creates the admin and editor\n- [ ] Login and the admin screen fit a 390 px wide screen with no sideways scrolling\n\n## Blocked by\n\nNone (can start immediately)\nEOF\ncat > $S/t02.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\nSpec: #1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe admin can create and edit an Update (a team news item) in an admin shell with persistent navigation. The title becomes an automatic slug that stays unique. The editor shows a Markdown preview that is sanitized, and every save shows a success or error message. New updates are always drafts and are visible only in the admin console.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The admin can create an update with a title and Markdown body; it is saved as a draft with author and created/updated timestamps\n- [ ] The slug is generated from the title, and a second update with the same title gets a different unique slug\n- [ ] The admin can edit an update and the change persists across a server restart\n- [ ] The editor shows a Markdown preview, and a body containing a script tag or an onerror attribute does not execute in the preview\n- [ ] A success message follows a good save and an error message follows a bad one (for example an empty title)\n- [ ] The admin navigation is visible on every admin screen\n- [ ] Every form carries a CSRF token and a POST without one is rejected\n- [ ] Anonymous visitors are redirected to login on these routes\n- [ ] The editor screen fits 390 px wide with no sideways scrolling\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #2 (T01: Log in and out)\nEOF\ncat > $S/t03.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\nSpec: #1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe admin can publish and unpublish an update, and `cms publish` renders only published updates into a static site: a home page listing updates newest first with a last-updated date, a purple and white CSS-only banner header, and relative paths only. `cms deploy` pushes the result to GitHub Pages, so a fan can open the live site and see the published update. A short runbook explains publish and deploy for whoever holds the admin role. This is the thin end-to-end path from write to live.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The admin can publish a draft and unpublish a published update, and the status persists across a server restart\n- [ ] `cms publish` exports only published updates; drafts and unpublished updates never appear in the exported files\n- [ ] Re-running `cms publish` after an unpublish removes that update from the exported site\n- [ ] The exported home page lists published updates newest first, each with its last-updated date\n- [ ] The exported site contains no root-absolute paths in href or src attributes, and all internal links resolve\n- [ ] Update bodies in the export are sanitized, so a script tag and an onerror attribute do not execute\n- [ ] The public site uses the purple and white look with a banner header and has no sideways scrolling at 390 px\n- [ ] After `cms deploy`, the Pages URL over HTTPS shows at least one published update\n- [ ] A short runbook describes publish and deploy step by step\n- [ ] Publish and unpublish are POST forms with CSRF tokens\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #3 (T02: Admin writes update drafts)\nEOF\ncat > $S/t04.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\nSpec: #1\n\n## What to build\n\nEditors become draft-only. An editor can create updates, edit any draft, and delete only their own drafts; they cannot publish, unpublish, or edit or delete published content. The admin can delete published content after a confirm step, and the next `cms publish` removes it from the site. Any admin-only action an editor tries leads to a clear \"not allowed\" screen, and anonymous visitors go to login.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An editor can create an update, and it is saved as a draft\n- [ ] An editor can edit any draft, including one written by someone else\n- [ ] An editor can delete their own draft but gets a refusal when deleting another editor's draft\n- [ ] An editor cannot publish or unpublish, and cannot edit or delete published content (403 or redirect to the refused screen)\n- [ ] The admin can delete published content after a confirm step; deleted content is gone after the next `cms publish`\n- [ ] Every admin-only route returns 403 or a redirect for an editor, and redirects an anonymous visitor to login (tests cover every such route)\n- [ ] The refused screen explains what is not allowed and fits 390 px wide\n- [ ] All new forms carry a CSRF token and reject a POST without one\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #3 (T02: Admin writes update drafts)\nEOF\ncat > $S/t05.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\nSpec: #1\n\n## What to build\n\nPages (Schedule, Roster, Results/Record, History, About/Contact) work like updates: same fields, draft and publish rules, and permissions. In addition, each page has a nav order set by the admin. Published pages become the public navigation in the exported site, in nav order, and each page shows its last-updated date.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An editor can create and edit a page as a draft, and only the admin can publish, unpublish, or delete it\n- [ ] A page has the same fields as an update (title, auto slug, sanitized Markdown, status, author, timestamps) plus a nav order that only the admin can set\n- [ ] Create, edit, publish, unpublish, and delete for pages all persist across a server restart\n- [ ] After `cms publish`, published pages appear in the navigation of every exported page, in nav order; drafts do not\n- [ ] An exported page shows its last-updated date\n- [ ] The navigation uses relative paths only and every nav link resolves\n- [ ] Page forms carry CSRF tokens and editors get the refused screen on admin-only page actions\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #4 (T03: Publish an update to the live site)\n- #5 (T04: Editors are draft-only)\nEOF\ncat > $S/t06.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\nSpec: #1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe admin console gets a dashboard that shows counts (drafts, published updates, pages) and a content list of updates and pages that can be filtered by status and by type, for both admin and editor.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The dashboard shows counts of drafts, published updates, and pages that match the data\n- [ ] The content list shows updates and pages together with title, type, status, author, and last-updated date\n- [ ] The list filters by status (draft or published) and by type (update or page), and the filters combine\n- [ ] A filter with no matches shows a clear empty message\n- [ ] Both admin and editor can see the dashboard and list, and anonymous visitors are redirected to login\n- [ ] The dashboard and list fit 390 px wide with no sideways scrolling\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #6 (T05: Pages with nav order)\nEOF\ncat > $S/t07.md <<'EOF'\n## Parent\n\nSpec: #1\n\n## What to build\n\nThe admin can manage users: create a user with an email, name, role, and starting password; change a user's role; and deactivate a user, who then cannot log in. Exactly one admin exists at all times, so a second admin can never be created by changing a role, and the admin cannot demote or deactivate themselves. A hand-over action promotes another user to admin and demotes the current admin in one step. Editors cannot reach any of this.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] The admin can create a user with a role, and the new user can log in; their password is stored as an argon2 hash\n- [ ] The admin can change a user's role between editor and a permitted value without ever producing two active admins\n- [ ] The admin can deactivate a user, and that user can no longer log in but keeps authorship of their content\n- [ ] The admin cannot demote or deactivate themselves outside of hand-over\n- [ ] Hand-over promotes the chosen user and demotes the current admin in one step, leaving exactly one admin\n- [ ] An editor gets 403 or a redirect on every user-management route, and anonymous visitors are redirected to login\n- [ ] All user-management forms carry CSRF tokens and reject a POST without one\n- [ ] The user list and forms fit 390 px wide with no sideways scrolling\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #5 (T04: Editors are draft-only)\nEOF\nmk \"T01: Log in and out\" $S/t01.md && mk \"T02:
